Week 2 build write-up

# Agent environments

## What an environment is
State, observations, actions, dynamics. The reward is a separate claim about what matters.

## Partial observability (POMDP)
When the agent cannot see the full state it must maintain a belief and sometimes act to gather information. Measurement can be an action with a cost.

## Attention as a hidden variable
Learners do not read everything shown to them. Attention gates learning and drains with fatigue.

# Evaluating agents

## pass@k vs pass^k
pass@k: any of k runs succeeds. pass^k: all k succeed. Reliability is what deployment needs.

## Proxy vs direct measures
A quiz score is a proxy. Retention a week later is closer to the thing itself.

args.text:
## Evaluation
We evaluate reliability with **pass^k**, not pass@k. Here, pass^k means **all k runs succeed**, which is stricter than pass@k (where any one of k runs succeeding is enough). Because the build is about dependable behavior, pass^k better matches the goal.

Planned protocol: run the agent on **at least 3 random seeds**. For each seed, execute the same task/setup and mark the run as pass or fail according to the task completion criterion. Then report pass^k for the chosen k over those runs. With 3 seeds, pass^3 is 1 only if all three runs succeed; otherwise it is 0. This makes the evaluation easy to interpret as a reliability check rather than a best-case score.

I should also briefly note the exact success condition used for a pass, the number of seeds, and any major failure modes observed.

args.text:
## Submission-ready version

### What I built
I built a study-assistant agent that helps a student prepare for Friday’s build while working at their computer. The agent gathers assignment requirements, checks readings and notes, explains concepts, drafts missing write-up sections, and checks understanding with short quizzes.

### Environment definition
The environment is the student’s computer workflow during a 90-minute study session.
- **State:** course files, readings, notes, calendar events, unread messages, and hidden learner variables such as attention and understanding.
- **Observations:** on-screen content, student messages, quiz results, note contents, assignment details, and course announcements.
- **Actions:** open/search files, assign readings, send explanations or direct answers, append to notes, run quizzes, and schedule study blocks.
- **Dynamics:** the student may learn from instruction, attention changes over time, and understanding is only partially observable.

### Evaluation
We evaluate reliability using **pass^k** rather than pass@k. **pass^k** means that **all k runs must succeed**, while pass@k only requires that at least one of the k runs succeed. Because this build cares about dependable behavior, pass^k is the better metric.

Our evaluation protocol is to run the agent on **at least 3 random seeds** using the same task setup each time. Each run is marked pass or fail according to whether the task is completed successfully. We then report **pass^3**, which is 1 only if all three runs succeed and 0 otherwise. We also report the success criterion, the number of seeds used, and any notable failure modes.
